rationale: Greek loanword πρωτοπολίτης 'first-citizen, leading citizen of a city.' Standard Sasanian-era term for urban notables, paired here with ϩⲏⲅⲉⲙⲱⲛ 'governors' as the civic-administrative class assembled around the apostle.
Disability-term paired with ⲕⲁⲕϩⲁⲡⲉ 'humpbacked' as the doublet of bodily disfigurement (lines 21, 30). Etymology likely related to ⲗⲟⲥ/ⲗⲱϣ 'be maimed, mutilated.' Confidence moderate.

Coptic ⲕⲁⲕⲏⲡⲉ 'crippled, deformed' with Lycopolitan epenthetic ϩ. Recurs lines 21 and 30 in the doublet ⲕⲁⲕϩⲁⲡⲉ ⲛⲉⲗⲟⲩⲥⲉ 'humpbacked and maimed' describing the foul-bodied elect. Likely a curvature/spinal-deformity term.
Possibly Greek loanword κυρτός 'humped, curved' or κορτός 'lame.' Modifier in the disfigurement-list of line 21 (ⲏ ⲁ(?) ⲛⲕⲩⲣⲧ). Confidence low; transcription itself is marked uncertain by editor.

Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲣ̄- + ϩⲉⲗ. Likely from a derisive-speech root (cf. ϩⲉⲗ-ϩⲏⲗ 'jeer, mock'). Paired with ⲥⲱⲃⲉ 'laughter' in line 32 as the doublet of derisive reception. The cosmopolitan/noble bystanders express their contempt through 'laughter and mockery.'

Verb in line 28 governing the elect's joyful approach to the apostle. Possibly Lyc. reflex of ϣⲱⲃⲉ 'leap, exchange' or related quick-motion verb. The elect, crying out from his joy, hastens/leaps to render homage. Confidence low.
Substantival relative on ⲧⲁⲙⲉ 'announce, make known.' Functions in line 6 as identifier of the teacher's truth-utterance: 'this is what proclaims (truth), my Lord.'
Lycopolitan ⲭ for ϫ; = Sahidic ϫⲡⲓⲟ 'shame, reprove, censure, refute.' Standard ethical-judicial verb. Line 7: 'he who shall reprove [...]'.
